bib.title: Demystifying Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in LLMs

question: Under what conditions do long chain-of-thought reasoning behaviours emerge and become stable in LLMs trained with SFT and RL?
hypothesis: Long CoT SFT gives a higher ceiling and better RL initialization than short CoT, and reward shaping plus verifiable-signal scaling are needed to stabilize and extend RL-driven CoT growth; base models already contain latent skills such as error validation.
contributions: SFT scaling and RL-initialization comparison of long vs short CoT
Cosine length-scaling reward with N-gram repetition penalty and per-reward discount factors
Scaling verifiable reward with noisy web-extracted (WebInstruct) data via filtering and rule-based verifier
Analysis of RL from base model and pretraining-data origins of long CoT behaviours

method.summary: Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-Math-7B are SFT-ed on rejection-sampled long CoT distilled from QwQ-32B-Preview (or short CoT from Qwen2.5-Math-72B-Instruct), then trained with PPO in OpenRLHF using a rule-based outcome verifier. Reward variants (classic, cosine length-scaling, repetition penalty, discount factors), context sizes, noisy WebInstruct data and direct RL from base are ablated and evaluated on MATH-500, AIME 2024, TheoremQA and MMLU-Pro-1k.
method.task: RL and SFT for long chain-of-thought mathematical and STEM reasoning

datasets.name: MATH train prompts
datasets.split: full train split (SFT and RL prompt set)
datasets.preprocessing: Rejection sampling: N candidates per prompt (N in {32,64,128,192,256} long; {32,64,128,256} short), keep correct

datasets.name: WebInstruct-462k
datasets.split: Filtered: ~189k responses over 115k prompts; RL uses 30k sampled prompts
datasets.preprocessing: Short-form answer extraction by Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, rejection sampling with 2 QwQ-32B-Preview responses per prompt; unfiltered SFT uses one unfiltered response

models.name: Llama-3.1-8B
models.context: RL: prompt 2048 + gen 14336 (16K); SFT context length 128K

models.name: Qwen2.5-Math-7B
models.context: pretraining 4096; RoPE theta x10 for long CoT

other.use: model-based verifier given reference solution and last 20 lines of CoT
Sec 5.2 text names it as the model-based verifier; App E.6 names Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (inconsistent)
Action Prompting construction of long CoT (o1-mini for reflection)

training.objective: SFT on rejection-sampled CoT; PPO with outcome reward (classic +1; cosine length reward with exceed penalty re=-10; N-gram repetition penalty P=-0.05, N=40); separate gamma per reward type in GAE, lambda=1
training.batch_size: SFT 256; RL 512 prompts rollout and train batch (Qwen direct RL: 1024, train 128)
training.steps: RL 100-160 iterations read from figures; episodes 4 or 8 or 16 or 20 per run
training.tokens: SFT scaling 0.1B to 10B tokens (read from Fig 1 axis); approx 200k SFT samples in Table 1
training.seeds: evaluation averaged over at least 4 random seeds; training seeds not stated

other.framework: OpenRLHF with Flash Attention 2, ZeRO/DeepSpeed, micro batch size 1
other.cosine_reward: r0c=+2, rLc=+1, r0w=-10, rLw=0, re=-10 (default); cosine CosFn(t,T,min,max)=min+0.5(max-min)(1+cos(t*pi/T))
other.GAE: lambda=1, gamma=1 default; best gamma_c=1, gamma_p=0.99
other.Qwen direct RL: rewards correct +1, wrong -0.5, no answer -1; lambda 0.95; 20 episodes; gen 3072

inference.decoding: sampling; greedy (t=0) for direct RL from Qwen2.5-Math-7B
inference.temperature: 0.7 default; 1.0 for QwQ distillation; 0 for base-model RL eval
inference.max_tokens: 16,384 default; 4096 for direct RL from base
inference.samples: Averaged over at least 4 seeds; 16 responses per prompt for AIME 2024

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of answers judged correct by SymEval

metrics.name: keyword rate
metrics.definition: frequency of reflection keywords wait, recheck, alternatively, retry, however

eval.protocol: At least 4 random seeds; 16 samples per AIME prompt; some RL experiments used an earlier version of the grader.

prompts.text: Given the following last 20 lines of the LLM response to a math question and the reference solution to that question, evaluate if the LLM response is correct based only on the LLM's final answer. LLM response (last 20 lines): ... {out} Reference solution: {ref} Explain your thought process step-by-step before responding with 'Judgement: <correct/wrong/not_found>'
Problem: {Problem} Solution: {Solution} Based on the Problem and the Solution, extract a short final answer that is easy to check.

prompts.purpose: Action Prompting: clarify, decompose, solution step, reflection, answer templates
prompts.text: You are a very talented mathematics professor.

results.claim: Long CoT SFT keeps improving on MATH-500 past 70% accuracy at 3.5B SFT tokens; short CoT SFT saturates below 55%.
results.setup: Llama-3.1-8B SFT on MATH-prompt data distilled from QwQ-32B-Preview (long) vs Qwen2.5-Math-72B-Instruct (short); N in {32..256} candidates per prompt; MATH-500
results.quote: long CoT SFT achieves over 70% accuracy and has yet to plateau even at 3.5B tokens

results.claim: RL on top of long CoT SFT adds over 3% absolute on MATH-500; short CoT SFT models gain almost nothing from RL.
results.setup: Llama-3.1-8B, PPO, rule-based verifier on MATH train, 4 epochs, 4 samples per prompt, cosine reward with repetition penalty
results.quote: RL can improve long CoT SFT models by over 3% absolute

results.claim: Emergent long CoT distilled from QwQ-32B-Preview beats constructed (Action Prompting) long CoT on MMLU-Pro-1k after SFT+RL.
results.setup: Llama-3.1-8B, ~200k SFT samples, MATH train prompts, same RL as Sec 3.2
results.note: Emergent SFT+RL MATH-500 59.4, AIME 4.0, TheoremQA 25.2; constructed SFT+RL 52.4, 2.7, 21.0
results.table: Table 1, row SFT+RL Emergent, column MMLU Pro-1k

results.claim: Cosine Reward (length-aware, sparse, with exceed-length penalty) stabilizes CoT length growth and training accuracy versus the Classic +1 reward, which drove CoTs to the context limit and collapsed accuracy.
results.setup: Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-Math-7B long CoT SFT, PPO, 16K context, MATH train
results.note: No single headline number; shown in curves only (Fig 4, 5).
results.quote: We found that the Cosine Reward significantly stabilized the length scaling behavior of the models under RL

results.claim: If the correct-answer reward rises with length (r0c < rLc) CoT length grows explosively; lower correct-to-wrong reward ratio yields longer CoT.
results.setup: Llama-3.1-8B, Rewards A/B/C in Fig 9 (A: r0c=0, rLc=10; B: 6/5; C: 10/9)
results.quote: if the reward for a correct answer increases with CoT length (rc 0 < rc L), the CoT length increases explosively

results.claim: With a 16K context, performance was worse than with 8K at equal training samples, suggesting larger contexts need more RL compute.
results.setup: Llama-3.1-8B, cosine reward + repetition penalty, context 4K/8K/16K, same number of samples
results.quote: we observed performance was better under 8K than 16K

results.claim: With enough compute the length reward is hacked by repetition and branching ('alternatively') falls; an N-gram repetition penalty (P=-0.05, N=40) mitigates it and gives shorter CoTs and better downstream accuracy.
results.setup: Llama-3.1-8B, cosine reward with and without repetition penalty, 8 episodes, 16 samples, 2 epochs
results.quote: Length rewards will be hacked with enough compute (Figure 10), but this can be mitigated using a repetition penalty.

results.claim: Best discount-factor setting is correctness gamma 1.0 and repetition gamma 0.99 (MATH-500 58.0 vs SFT init 50.4); too-low correctness discount hurts badly (0.99/0.99 gives 47.9 and AIME 0.2).
results.setup: Llama-3.1-8B, cosine + repetition penalty, separate gamma per reward type via modified GAE, lambda=1
results.table: Table 5, row correctness discount 1.000, repetition discount 0.99, column MATH-500

results.claim: Mixing 50% MATH and 50% WebInstruct for long CoT SFT gives best average accuracy after SFT+RL (32.1) versus 100% MATH (30.8) and 100% WebIT (28.1).
results.setup: Llama-3.1-8B, QwQ-32B-Preview distillation, WebInstruct data one unfiltered response per prompt, RL on MATH
results.table: Table 2, row 50% MATH + 50% WebIT SFT + RL, column AVG

results.claim: Adding WebInstruct to SFT lifts MMLU-Pro-1k from 32.0 to 41.1 (100% WebIT SFT) but lowers MATH-500 to 41.2.
results.table: Table 2, row 100% WebIT SFT, column MMLU Pro-1k

results.claim: RL with a rule-based verifier on prompts filtered for short-form answers is best overall from noisy web data (MMLU-Pro-1k 41.4, TheoremQA 28.1); rule-based on unfiltered data is worst (MATH-500 45.4).
results.setup: Llama-3.1-8B SFT on ~189k responses over 115k prompts; RL 30k prompts, 4 responses each
results.note: Filtered rule-based: MATH-500 48.6, AIME 3.3, TheoremQA 28.1. Unfiltered rule-based: 45.4, 3.3, 25.9, 35.1. Unfiltered model-based 47.9, 3.5, 26.2, 40.4.
results.table: Table 3, row Filtered Rule-Based, column MMLU Pro-1k

results.claim: RL directly from Qwen2.5-Math-7B raises accuracy but does not increase self-validation keyword rates (wait, recheck, alternatively, retry, however); recheck already exists in the base model.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-Math-7B, PPO, ~8k MATH level 3-5 questions, greedy decoding, max 4096 tokens
results.quote: nor effectively incentivize other reflection patterns

results.claim: Output length in direct RL from the base model never exceeds the base model's initial length, and rises as KL to the base drops, so length growth may reflect the KL penalty rather than learned long CoT.
results.quote: never exceeds the initial length of the base model

results.claim: Qwen2.5-Math-7B: SFT+RL from long CoT SFT reaches average 49.7 versus 41.0 for direct RL from base and 47.3 for SFT alone.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-Math-7B, QwQ-32B-Preview distillation 32 candidates per prompt, PPO with cosine reward + repetition penalty, 8 samples per prompt, 8 epochs, RoPE theta x10
results.note: Text: surpasses RL from base by 8.7% on average and SFT init by 2.6%. Grader earlier-version caveat in App E.1.
results.table: Table 4, row SFT + RL, column AVG

results.claim: Direct RL from the base model lifts MATH-500 from 52.0 to 77.4 but MMLU-Pro-1k only from 2.4 to 19.7, versus 38.5 with long CoT SFT.
REINFORCE++ was significantly less stable than PPO in this setup; authors caution it may be untuned.
results.quote: we found it to be significantly more unstable than PPO, leading to lower training accuracies (Figure 13)

results.claim: Discussion-forum threads in OpenWebMath show long-CoT-like dialogue (branching, backtracking, correction), hypothesised as a source of long CoT in pretraining data.
results.setup: MinHash search of OpenWebMath with GPT-4o-generated 'aha' phrases; Perplexity.ai web search
results.quote: This raises the intriguing possibility that long CoT originated from human dialogue

limits: RL from Qwen2.5-Math-7B did not reproduce DeepSeek-R1-style emergent behaviour; authors suggest model size (7B) or overexposure to MATH-like data, untested (Sec 6.3, 7.1).
Could not scale to 32B because the GPU requirement was too large (Sec 7.2).
REINFORCE++ instability may be due to untuned setup, so no general claim (Sec 7.3).
Only outcome rewards and mainly 8B/7B models and mostly math prompts; some RL experiments used an earlier grader version (App E.1).
Results mostly read from curves, few headline numbers; no hardware or compute stated; pretraining-origin hypothesis (forums) is speculative and untested.
Interactions between repetition penalty strength, training accuracy and cosine reward left to future work (Sec 4.5).

terms.definition: an extended sequence of reasoning tokens that not only exhibits a larger-than-usual token length but also demonstrates more sophisticated behaviors such as branching, backtracking, error validation and correction
length-dependent sparse reward: correct CoTs get higher reward than wrong, shorter correct get more than longer correct, shorter wrong get larger penalties than longer wrong

code.snippet: CosFn(t, T, eta_min, eta_max) = eta_min + 1/2 (eta_max - eta_min)(1 + cos(t*pi/T))
A_t = sum_{l=0}^{L} sum_m gamma_m^l r_{m,t+l} - V(s_t)  (GAE with per-reward-type gamma, lambda=1)
N-gram repetition penalty: slide an N-gram window over the sequence; if the n-gram was seen, set r[t]=P for all its positions
